[0] At Apple's September event today, the company unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo — but not a base model iPhone 18. Here's why.

[1] The iPhone 18 base model is expected to launch in early 2027, as Apple has changed its product release schedule.

[2] You might typically refer to today's Apple event as the "iPhone 18 launch."

[3] But Apple did something today that probably surprised a lot of people — it didn't announce the iPhone 18, at least not the base model.

[4] Instead, Apple only unveiled three new premium iPhones: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.

[5] This flagship lineup is a notable departure from Apple's usual approach, which typically involves releasing a new base-model iPhone alongside the Pro versions. However, this change had been foreshadowed by reports as early as May 2025.

[6] According to multiple reports, the three new iPhone models Apple announced today will be joined by three more additions in early 2027:

  • [7] iPhone 18
  • [8] iPhone 18e
  • [9] iPhone Air 2

[10] So the base iPhone 18 isn't cancelled — it's just arriving later than usual.

[11] Why the change?

[12] One explanation is that Apple wants to expand its iPhone lineup further than ever before with new form factors like the foldable-screen Duo, and doesn't want to cram too many products into a single fall launch. Splitting its major iPhone releases between fall and spring cycles could therefore make more sense.

[13] Another possible reason is that Apple anticipated the current memory shortage and knew it would struggle to meet demand if it launched the base iPhone 18, the Pro models, and the Duo simultaneously.

[14] Either way, the iPhone 18 will arrive — just not until early 2027.

[15] What do you think of the company's strategy to stagger the iPhone 18 lineup? Let us know in the comments.
